businessRules.rule: A suspension is raised from an incident already recorded, and carries the reason, the incident it arises from, and the proposed number of days. A sanction with no recorded incident behind it cannot be defended.

The Principal approves it and sets the start date and the return date. This approval is not configurable to a lower role. The Super Admin configures the permission but cannot set it below the Principal.

Where the student has an open special educational need or safeguarding record, that record is reviewed before the suspension is approved. Behaviour is sometimes a symptom of something the school already knows about, and approving without looking is how a child in difficulty is punished for being in difficulty.
The guardian is notified of the reason, the dates, and what is required before the student returns. A family told only that the child is suspended cannot meet a condition nobody stated.

A suspended student is not withdrawn and is not absent. The place is held, so they remain on the section roster, remain in class counts, and continue to be invoiced. The school is holding a place it is not letting the child occupy, and it charges for it.

Attendance is coded suspended rather than absent. No absence alert is sent, and the days are not counted as unexplained absence. Without this state a suspended student is marked absent and their guardian is alerted daily that the child did not come in, when the school sent them home.
Whether a suspended student may sit an examination falling within the period is decided at approval and recorded. Where they do not sit, the paper is recorded as an exam absence and classified there.
The enrolment continues throughout. Nothing about the student's record, their placement or their fee position changes because of the suspension, beyond the state itself.
On the return date the state reverts automatically and attendance is expected again. A suspension that has to be ended by hand is a suspension that will occasionally run on.
The Principal may end the suspension early, with a reason, and the guardian is notified. The state reverts from that date.
The suspension is held on the student's record and is visible to the coordinator. Repeated suspensions are visible together, since a pattern is what leads to an expulsion.
A suspension is never deleted. A recommendation that was returned or refused stays on the record.
Every raising, approval, early ending and change is written to the audit log with the reason, the dates and the approver.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Student → Suspension approval → Review the support record

basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval and the examination decision. No lower role can give it.

basicFlow.userAction: Notifies the guardian of the reason, the dates and what is required before the student returns.

Holds the student in a Suspended state, codes attendance as suspended rather than absent, sends no absence alert and counts no day as unexplained absence.
Keeps the student on the section roster and in class counts, and continues to invoice, since the place is being held.
Reverts the state on the return date and expects attendance again, without anybody having to end it.

basicFlow.userAction: Ends the suspension before the return date, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Reverts the state from that date and notifies the guardian.

departures.aspect: Suspended is neither absent nor withdrawn
departures.requirement: No route treats a suspended student as absent or as having left. Attendance codes the day suspended, alerts are suppressed, the roster and class counts are unchanged, and invoicing continues.
The Principal's approval is not configurable to a lower role by any route, including the Super Admin's permission configuration.
Where an open support record exists, approval is blocked until it is reviewed. Approving without looking is how a child in difficulty is punished for being in difficulty.
The state reverts on the return date without anybody ending it, because a suspension that has to be ended by hand will occasionally run on.
The family is told the reason, the dates and the conditions of return together, and a failure to reach them is reported so the school can telephone.
Suspensions are retained 7 years, since a pattern of them is what an expulsion rests on.

openQuestions.question: The Super Admin is listed as deciding the approval permission, but the approval is also stated as not configurable to a lower role. As modelled the Super Admin configures the permission and cannot set it below the Principal, but the two statements need reconciling.
openQuestions.assumption: Modelled as a floor at the Principal.

openQuestions.question: Should a teacher see the reason for a suspension, or only that the student is suspended and until when?
openQuestions.assumption: Only the dates as modelled. A teacher may need the reason to manage the return.

openQuestions.question: Is there a maximum length beyond which a suspension becomes something else?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. A long suspension is an expulsion in practice.

openQuestions.question: Does a suspended student have any right to work set for them during the period?
openQuestions.assumption: Not modelled, and the document does not raise it.

openQuestions.question: Does the school ever refund or reduce fees for a suspension period?
openQuestions.assumption: No. The place is held and billing continues (BR-5). Families will ask.

openQuestions.question: How many suspensions constitute the pattern that leads to an expulsion?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The report shows the count but nothing acts on it.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
